clue.text: Help cure an eccentric creature of folklore

indicators.note: something eccentric is odd and out of line, so the preceding words are put into a strange new order

blocks.note: the three words supply every letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks for help curing a strange creature from the old tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A leprechaun is a mischievous little fairy shoemaker in Irish folk tradition.

clue.text: Ignore amorous advance with vocal farewell

indicators.note: vocal means spoken out, so the word for farewell counts only for how it is pronounced

blocks.note: to make a pass is to make a romantic approach
bye is a casual goodbye, and the preposition is pronounced identically

explanation.surface: Someone rebuffs a romantic approach with a spoken goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass someone by is to overlook them or take no notice, a phrasal verb for disregarding.

clue.text: Made dark plot, gestured to have leader brought down

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for gestured is shifted one place lower in this down entry, a small rearrangement

blocks.note: a garden plot or flower bed
to mime is to act out with gestures

explanation.surface: A conspirator's dark plot is signalled by gestures, with the boss toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, bringing the leader down means sliding the first letter one place lower, not removing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedim is an old literary verb for making something dim or obscure; the past tense matches.

clue.text: Presented way over the hill

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
over the hill is an idiom for elderly

explanation.surface: Someone was shown the path across the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the hill' looks like directions after 'way', but it is an idiom for old.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is staged has been mounted or put on for an audience, as a show is presented.

clue.text: Corresponding but never meeting

blocks.note: first meaning: analogous, matching in some way
second meaning: lines that run side by side for ever without crossing

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests pen pals who write to each other yet never meet in person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes analogous situations and also geometric lines that keep equal distance apart without intersecting.

clue.text: Crust of snow at front on vehicle

indicators.note: at front asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: its opening letter
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A frozen layer of snow has formed on the front of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the dried hard covering that forms over a healing wound.

clue.text: Go over a time one’s expected back

indicators.note: going back means the abbreviation for an expected time is read from right to left

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
per means a, as in once per day
estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: Someone is told to review the hour by which they should be home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go over' looks like a phrase meaning review, but 'Go' alone is the definition and 'over' is a cricket term.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that operates is working or running, just as a device can be said to go.

clue.text: Left university commitments to follow work prospects

indicators.note: to follow places the earlier words after the next piece rather than before it

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
port is the left side of a ship
a common abbreviation
ties are bonds or obligations

explanation.surface: A graduate leaves college duties behind to pursue career openings.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportunities are chances or openings for the future, the same as good prospects in a career.

clue.text: Dazed state outside hospital block

indicators.note: outside means the word for a dazed state wraps around the hospital letter

blocks.note: a trance is a half-conscious state
H is the abbreviation on hospital signs

explanation.surface: A stunned patient stands outside a hospital building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Block' sounds like a building beside the hospital, but it means a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tranche is a portion or slice, especially of money or shares, issued as one block.

clue.text: Writer‘s novel surmised penned after leaving Italy

indicators.note: after leaving says the country's letter departs from the fodder before it is rearranged
novel means new, so the letters take on a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An author's book was guessed to have been written once they had left Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the writer's book but is the anagram signal; the Italy letter goes before the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Spenser was the Elizabethan poet who wrote The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Freezing cold PM after exercise class no good

indicators.note: after places the prime minister's name behind the class abbreviation

blocks.note: PE is physical education, the school exercise class
Rishi Sunak was UK Prime Minister from 2022 to 2024
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister turns up chilled after a useless gym session.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishing is informal British for bitterly cold, as in a perishing winter morning.

clue.text: No space in white book

indicators.note: no here means without, so the printer's space unit is taken away

blocks.note: an en is a printer's unit of space
albumen is egg white

explanation.surface: A blank white book has no room left in it.
explanation.walkthrough: ALBUMEN minus EN leaves ALBUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a blank-paged book for keeping photographs, stamps or autographs.

clue.text: Rough diamond meeting Yankee

blocks.note: rock is slang for a diamond
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An uncut gemstone comes face to face with an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough diamond' reads as a phrase for a good-hearted but uncouth person; 'Rough' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky road or rocky patch is uneven and difficult, so rocky describes rough terrain or times.

clue.text: Cut a line that’s bitten by sea cat

indicators.note: something bitten is held in the jaws, so the sea and cat words close around a line

blocks.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea, and a lion is a big cat
A as written plus L, the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A sea lion has taken a bite out of a fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sea cat' suggests a sea lion, but it is two separate words, with A L slotted between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A medallion is a small round piece of meat, such as a medallion of beef, a butcher's cut.

clue.text: Unsure of Parisian cutting corners

indicators.note: to corner something is to trap it, so the word for cutting hems in the French word

blocks.note: incisive remarks are sharp and cutting
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Someone is doubtful about a Parisian who takes shortcuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting corners' reads as one idiom for skimping, but 'corners' is a verb meaning traps.
explanation.definitionFit: An indecisive person hesitates and cannot make up their mind, which is to be unsure.

clue.text: After cutting introduction, Freudian slips not broadcast

indicators.note: cutting the introduction means the opening letter of the next word is dropped
something that slips loses its place, so the remaining letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Revealing slips of the tongue were edited out before transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freudian slips' is a familiar phrase, but 'slips' is a verb here, telling the letters to move.
explanation.definitionFit: An unaired programme or episode has never been shown on television or radio.

clue.text: Infrequency of two military groups being on headland

indicators.note: being on, in a down entry, puts the earlier pieces above the later one

blocks.note: RA is the Royal Artillery and RE the Royal Engineers, both British Army corps
a ness is a promontory, as in place names like Orford Ness

explanation.surface: Army units seldom appear stationed on a coastal promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Rareness is the quality of seldom happening or occurring, the noun matching infrequency.

clue.text: American chaps worn by the Spanish kids

indicators.note: what is worn by someone sits inside their clothing, so the Spanish article goes within the chaps

blocks.note: dude is American slang for a man
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Cowboys in leather chaps borrowed from Spanish riders, with children watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaps' and 'kids' both look like nouns for people; 'kids' is a verb meaning fools.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease or fool them, and to delude is likewise to deceive.

clue.text: Neighbourhood police officer, authoritarian

blocks.note: DI is a detective inspector
a strict person enforces rules firmly

explanation.surface: The local beat officer rules the area with an iron hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area or region of a town, such as a residential quarter.

clue.text: Digging on road regularly turned problem for uninformed person

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second one
turned means the word for problem is flipped and read backwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Roadworks have become a headache for someone who knows nothing about them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant or poorly educated person who lacks knowledge.

clue.text: Role taken on by another informant leader hides

indicators.note: hides means the letters are concealed inside the run of words before it

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A spy takes on a new part while the chief keeps something secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' belongs to the definition, not the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up someone's mantle is to assume a responsibility handed down by a predecessor.

clue.text: Collection notes perhaps received by auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is taken in by the ear

blocks.note: banknotes are an example of cash, hinted by perhaps

explanation.surface: Banknotes are handed to an accountant checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it simply means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a hidden store or hoard of items gathered together.

clue.text: I’m surprised there’s little pressure in bellows

indicators.note: in places the pressure letter inside the word for bellows

blocks.note: to bellow is to shout or cry out
P is the symbol for pressure, little as a single letter

explanation.surface: Someone is startled to find a weak puff of air in a fireplace bellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bellows' looks like the fireplace tool, but it is a verb meaning shouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cripes is a dated British exclamation of astonishment, standing for an expression of surprise.

clue.text: Article seen on island from over the pond

blocks.note: IOW is the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece appears about an island across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the article after the island. 'Over the pond' means across the Atlantic, in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Iowan describes someone or something from Iowa, a US state, and so from America.

clue.text: Heartlessly cheer defeat

indicators.note: heartlessly means without the heart, the central letter of the next word

blocks.note: a whoop is a loud cry of joy

explanation.surface: A callous fan jeers at a team's loss.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle O of WHOOP goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Whop is an informal variant of whup, to beat or thrash an opponent thoroughly.

clue.text: Recalled crime pinching bow, suspect mythological figure

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for crime is read backwards
pinching means taking hold of, so the reversed crime grips the bow

blocks.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
a bow is curved like an arc
sus is slang for suspect or suspicious

explanation.surface: A crime is remembered in which a suspect stole a bow from a figure of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is the beautiful youth of Greek myth who fell in love with his own reflection.

clue.text: Wound up with a loss of partner

indicators.note: wound means twisted or coiled, so the letters are wrapped into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bereaved person ends up overwhelmed by grief after losing their partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound up' reads as one phrase meaning upset; 'Wound' alone is the signal and 'up' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spousal is the adjective for things relating to a husband or wife, a marriage partner.

clue.text: King having holiday aboard cutter

indicators.note: aboard means on board inside, so the word for holiday sits within the royal letters

blocks.note: CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
leave is time off work

explanation.surface: A monarch takes a vacation on a small sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is also a small boat, which makes 'aboard' sit naturally in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy butcher's knife, a tool for chopping meat.
